log.msg: The judge earned its tier. Three parties, three numbers, and the decisive move was refusing to read the arguments first — count the characters on the first rendered line, two independent ways, and let every instrument be judged against that. The real finding was not a number but a POPULATION: taste read.js measure was a median over text BLOCKS, so a two-line caption and a forty-line article got one vote each, and it admitted <pre> and span.hljs-* as prose. Across ten routes it ran 24.4 to 254.3 and never came within 40 of the truth. probe.js arithmetic was fine at -2%. Fixed: code excluded (the exemption rules.js has had since the day it was written) and weighted by LINES, because the question is how long a line of this page is and a line is the unit.
